correctness.rationale: The renewal transform has successful-attempt transform p(√((r+s)/D)) and failed-attempt transform r(1−p(√((r+s)/D)))/(r+s). Equivalently the total transform is 1/(1+sA(s)), where A(s)=(1−p)/((r+s)p) at q=√((r+s)/D); expansion gives mean A(0) and variance A(0)^2−2A′(0), reproducing (1), with finite moments at positive r. The finite positive left-end density value c gives a strictly positive V with tail g/c and finite mean 1/c, even without moments of U; Fubini yields p=b/q. Differentiation of (2) gives (3). Independently, set x=qV, a=E(1−e^−x), d=Ex, u=E(xe^−x), v=E(x²e^−x). The expected collected kernel (5) is −v(d−u)+3(a−u)^2−(d−u−v)(a−u), which expands to m²G from (3), verifying the key pairing. For x>0 the two scalar inequalities follow by differentiating x−2+(x+2)e^−x and by H(0)=H′(0)=0, H″(0)=1, H‴(x)=xe^x>0. Since R is positive, R(x)S(y)>2R(x)>3−x even when 3−x is negative; hence the kernel is strictly negative for each positive pair. The small-q bound p/(1−p) follows from concavity of 1−p and tends to infinity. Changing variables to qu in the Laplace integrals and dominating by the finite density bound gives qp→c and −q²p′→c at infinity, so CV tends to 1 and strict decrease gives CV>1 at finite rates. Uniform interval targets satisfy the density hypothesis, with an empty second piece at the center and a uniform distance law at either boundary.
residual_risks: The reported numerical cases are only corroboration. The proof assumes independent redraws initially and at every reset and an absolutely continuous distance law with bounded nonincreasing version; it does not apply to quenched mixtures or atoms.

checked_sources: Méndez et al. §VII.B, uniform interval comparison
value.rationale: The theorem resolves a concrete rate-dependence question previously investigated numerically for the uniform interval and gives a checkable density criterion for other ensembles. Its strictly negative two-variable kernel applies uniformly to all positive mixture scales, with no moments of the distance assumed. This is a useful fluctuation result, including for off-center and boundary targets, not just a computation of the known renewal formula or of a single optimum.
residual_risks: The density criterion is sufficient only and does not classify rate behavior for arbitrary reset laws.
